blogs.title: When the Brain Forgets to Breathe: Unmasking Acquired Central Hypoventilation in Chiari Malformation
blogs.description: Explore the pathophysiology of 'Ondine's Curse' in adults with Chiari Type I, focusing on the dissociation between preserved voluntary breathing and failed automatic respiratory drive. This post analyzes why patients may suffer severe desaturation (down to 70%) without subjective dyspnea, discussing the interruption of afferent pathways to the cortex and the critical need to distinguish this from primary pulmonary or cardiac causes.

blogs.title: Choking Without a Cause: Why Dysphagia Should Trigger a Look Upwards
blogs.description: Challenge the reflexive workup for dysphagia that stops at gastroenterology and ENT. This post examines how lower cranial nerve compression in Chiari malformation mimics refractory GERD or structural esophageal lesions, emphasizing that choking affecting both solids and liquids equally—especially with normal endoscopy—is a red flag for brainstem pathology requiring neuroimaging.

blogs.title: The Crowded Foramen Magnum: How Historical Imaging Saved a Decade-Long Diagnostic Odyssey
blogs.description: Discuss the critical role of retrieving and re-interpreting old imaging studies in undiagnosed neurological conditions. Using this case as a template, this post reviews the subtle radiological signs of Chiari I on non-contrast CT (crowding, loss of CSF space) that are easily missed by non-specialists and argues for a 'second look' policy when clinical suspicion remains high despite negative modern workups.

blogs.title: Beyond Headaches: Decoding Atypical Scalp Pain and Allodynia in Posterior Fossa Pathology
blogs.description: Move past the classic Valsalva-induced occipital headache to discuss less recognized sensory phenomena like vertex allodynia ('hair-touch pain') and Burning Vertex Syndrome. This post explores the potential mechanisms linking cerebellar tonsillar descent to trigeminal/cervical sensory integration issues and offers guidance on recognizing these atypical presentations as part of the Chiari symptom profile.

blogs.title: Sleep Study Pitfalls: Why Your Type III Polysomnogram Might Miss Severe Central Apnea
blogs.description: Critique the limitations of outpatient sleep monitoring (Type III) in patients with suspected brainstem compression. This educational piece explains how the lack of EEG leads to underestimation of Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) by diluting event counts across wakeful hours, arguing why Type I studies with end-tidal CO2 monitoring are mandatory for accurate risk stratification in Chiari-associated respiratory failure.
